trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona Airport at 22:30. Take the Aerobus (€5.90 one-way) or the RENFE train (€4.60) to the city center. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Take a short stroll along the nearby Barceloneta beachfront promenade to decompress after your flight — it's lively at night in August. Grab a late-night snack from a nearby kiosk or 24-hour convenience store.

meals.dinner: Late-night bocadillo (sandwich) or kebab from a local takeaway near the hotel (~€4–6). Many spots near Barceloneta are open past midnight.

day_by_day.notes: Keep luggage light for the airport transfer. Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) upon arrival at the airport — it will save money throughout the trip. August in Barcelona is hot and humid; stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in to recover from travel. After a late breakfast, head to the iconic Sagrada Família (book tickets online in advance for ~€26 — the basic entry ticket). Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece, one of the world's most extraordinary examples of Modernista architecture. Walk around the exterior and surrounding park for free if budget is very tight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the metro to the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic). Wander through its medieval labyrinthine streets completely free of charge. Visit the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30 and after 17:30 on weekdays). Explore Plaça Reial and Plaça de Sant Jaume. Pop into any of the small local shops or browse the architecture at no cost.
day_by_day.evening: Head to El Born neighborhood, adjacent to the Gothic Quarter. Enjoy the vibrant bar scene — many bars offer €2–3 draft beers and free tapas during happy hour (roughly 18:00–20:00). Later, walk to the W Barcelona waterfront area near the hotel for nightlife. Check out beach clubs or open-air bars along Passeig Marítim that have free entry.

meals.breakfast: Café con leche and a croissant or tostada at a local bar near the hotel (~€3–4). Avoid tourist-facing cafés near the beach for breakfast.
meals.lunch: Menú del día (set lunch menu) at a local restaurant in the Gothic Quarter — typically includes starter, main, dessert, bread, and a drink for €10–13. Look for spots frequented by locals rather than tourists.
meals.dinner: Pan con tomate and shared tapas at a bar in El Born (~€8–12 per person). Try patatas bravas, croquetas, and jamón.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Gothic Quarter has uneven cobblestone streets. Book Sagrada Família tickets at least a few days in advance; they sell out fast in August. Keep an eye on your belongings in the Gothic Quarter, which is a known pickpocket area.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Park Güell (book timed entry tickets in advance — €10 for the Monumental Zone, or explore the free outer areas). Arrive early (around 08:00) to beat the August crowds and heat. Admire Gaudí's mosaic terraces, gingerbread gatehouses, and sweeping views over Barcelona. The free outer park paths and viaducts are equally impressive for architecture lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the metro to Passeig de Gràcia to walk the 'Block of Discord' (Manzana de la Discordia) — a free outdoor architecture tour featuring Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera. Admire the facades from the outside (entering Casa Batlló costs ~€35, so skip the interior to stay budget-friendly). Continue to Casa Milà (La Pedrera) and admire the exterior for free. Stop by Mercat de la Boqueria on La Rambla for a browse — grab fresh fruit or a snack from market stalls (~€2–3).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Barceloneta beachfront area near the hotel. Enjoy a sunset swim at Barceloneta Beach (free). As the sun sets, the beach bars (chiringuitos) come alive — grab a sangria or beer (~€4–5). Later, explore the nightlife in the El Poblenou neighborhood, a short walk from the hotel, which has a more local, less touristy bar scene. Many bars don't get busy until 23:00.

meals.breakfast: Freshly squeezed orange juice and a pastry from a local bakery or market stall (~€3–4).
meals.lunch: Bocadillo de jamón or empanada from the Boqueria market or a nearby takeaway (~€4–6). Eat standing at a market bar to save money.
meals.dinner: Paella or fideuà at a mid-range restaurant in Barceloneta (~€12–15 per person). Look for restaurants one block back from the beachfront to avoid tourist markup. Alternatively, grab a shawarma or falafel wrap near the hotel (~€5–7).

day_by_day.notes: August heat peaks in the afternoon (often 30–35°C). Plan outdoor walking for the morning and rest or visit air-conditioned spaces in the early afternoon. Carry a reusable water bottle — there are free drinking fountains throughout the city (Las Fuentes de Barcelona).

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro or bus to Montjuïc hill. Ride the Montjuïc Cable Car (Telefèric de Montjuïc, ~€12.70 round trip) or save money by taking Bus 150 (~€2.40 with T-Casual card). Explore Montjuïc Castle (€5 entry) for panoramic views over the city and port. Walk the castle ramparts and enjoy the architecture of this 17th-century fortress.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to explore the Montjuïc gardens — Jardins de Laribal and Jardí Botànic (€3.50 entry) are free or very cheap and beautifully landscaped. Walk down to the Fundació Joan Miró (€15 entry) if interested in art and architecture — the building itself by Josep Lluís Sert is an architectural gem. Alternatively, skip the entry and admire the exterior, then head to Poble Sec neighborhood at the foot of Montjuïc for a local afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: The Magic Fountain (Font Màgica de Montjuïc) puts on a free light and music show on Thursday–Sunday evenings in summer, starting around 21:30. Arrive early to grab a spot. Afterward, head to Poble Sec's Carrer de Blai — the 'pintxos street' — where you can eat pintxos (Basque-style tapas on bread) for €1–1.50 each at multiple bars. This is one of Barcelona's best budget food streets.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and tostada con tomate y aceite (toast with tomato and olive oil) at a bar in Poble Sec before heading up Montjuïc (~€3–4).
meals.lunch: Picnic on Montjuïc — buy supplies from a supermarket (Mercadona or Lidl) the night before: bread, cheese, cold cuts, fruit (~€5–7 total).
meals.dinner: Pintxos crawl on Carrer de Blai in Poble Sec — budget €8–12 for a satisfying dinner of pintxos and a drink at 2–3 different bars.

day_by_day.notes: The Magic Fountain show schedule can change — check the Barcelona city website (barcelona.cat) closer to the date to confirm times. Poble Sec is a great neighborhood to explore for a more authentic, non-touristy Barcelona experience. Wear sunscreen — Montjuïc is very exposed to the sun.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed final morning at Barceloneta Beach — enjoy a last swim and soak up the Mediterranean sun. Walk along the Passeig Marítim promenade toward the Port Olímpic area. Admire Frank Gehry's golden 'Fish' (Peix) sculpture and the modern Olympic Village architecture built for the 1992 Games — all viewable for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palau de la Música Catalana (exterior is a UNESCO-listed Modernista masterpiece — free to admire; guided tours cost ~€22 but the exterior alone is stunning). Walk through the El Born neighborhood one last time for souvenir shopping — La Casa dels Entrepans and small local shops offer better prices than La Rambla. Stop by the Born Cultural Centre (free entry) — a stunning 19th-century iron market building with archaeological ruins of the 1714 siege of Barcelona beneath a glass floor.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening — enjoy a farewell dinner in El Born or Barceloneta. Pack your bags and prepare for departure. If your flight is the next morning, consider a final walk along the illuminated beachfront at night, which is magical in August with the warm sea breeze.

meals.breakfast: Full Spanish breakfast at a local bar near the beach — café con leche, zumo de naranja (fresh orange juice), and tostada (~€5–7).
meals.lunch: Menú del día at a local restaurant in El Born (~€11–13) for a proper sit-down farewell lunch.
meals.dinner: Budget-friendly final dinner — try a falafel wrap or döner kebab near the hotel (~€5–7), or splurge slightly on a shared seafood plate at a Barceloneta restaurant (~€15–18 per person).

day_by_day.notes: If departing the next day, confirm checkout time with Aegean Bliss Resort and arrange luggage storage if needed. Keep metro T-Casual card topped up for the airport transfer. Total estimated daily budget (excluding accommodation): €30–50 per person per day, covering transport, entry fees, and meals when following budget tips throughout the itinerary.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival day — no morning activities scheduled. Flight UA lands at 22:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrival day — no afternoon activities scheduled. Use travel time to prepare.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Aerobus or a taxi (~30 min) to Aegean Bliss Resort on the Beachfront. Check in, freshen up, and take a short relaxing stroll along the Barceloneta beachfront promenade to unwind after your flight. Grab a light late-night bite near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at a nearby beachfront bar or 24-hour café near Barceloneta — try a simple bocadillo (Spanish sandwich) and a cold Estrella Damm beer. Budget ~€10–15.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you're arriving late at night. Pre-book your airport transfer if possible to avoid taxi queues. Confirm hotel check-in details for late arrival. Set alarms for an early start on Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a leisurely breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café. Then head to the Sagrada Família Guided Tour (pre-book skip-the-line tickets online). Spend 2–2.5 hours marveling at Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica — explore the Nativity and Passion facades, the soaring interior nave, and climb a tower for panoramic city views. The guided tour provides rich context about the architecture and symbolism.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Sagrada Família, walk or take the metro to the Gothic Quarter Walking Tour. Wander through Barcelona's medieval heart, discovering Roman ruins, Gothic cathedrals, hidden plazas like Plaça de Sant Felip Neri, and the Barcelona Cathedral. The tour typically lasts 1.5–2 hours. Afterward, explore freely — browse local shops and soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Head to El Born neighborhood (a short walk from the Gothic Quarter) for dinner and evening drinks. Explore the vibrant bar scene along Carrer del Parlament or Passeig del Born. Enjoy craft cocktails or local vermouth at a trendy bar before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Café de l'Acadèmia area or hotel breakfast — try a croissant, freshly squeezed orange juice, and café amb llet (coffee with milk). Budget ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Post-Gothic Quarter lunch at a mid-range restaurant in El Born — try 'Bar del Pla' for classic Catalan dishes like croquetes and patatas bravas. Budget ~€15–20.
meals.dinner: Dinner in El Born at a tapas restaurant — try 'El Xampanyet' for anchovies, cava, and house tapas. Budget ~€20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets well in advance — they sell out weeks ahead, especially in August. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Gothic Quarter tour. August is hot in Barcelona; carry water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Start with breakfast and then join the Tapas and Wine Tour in El Born. This guided food tour takes you through the trendy El Born neighborhood sampling traditional Catalan tapas — patatas bravas, jamón ibérico, pan con tomate, and more — paired with local wines and cava. Tours typically run mid-morning to early afternoon (~3 hours) and are a fantastic way to understand local food culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the food tour (and likely well-fed!), take a relaxing afternoon at Barceloneta Beach, just a short walk from your hotel at Aegean Bliss Resort. Swim in the Mediterranean, rent a sun lounger, or simply enjoy the vibrant beach atmosphere. Consider renting a bike along the beachfront promenade for a scenic coastal ride toward Port Olímpic.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a live performance at the Palau de la Música Catalana — a UNESCO-listed modernista masterpiece designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Check the evening concert schedule in advance and book tickets online. The stunning stained-glass ceiling and ornate interior make even a short concert an unforgettable architectural and cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery — try a freshly baked ensaïmada pastry and coffee. Budget ~€8–10.
meals.lunch: Included in the Tapas and Wine Tour (confirm with tour operator). If not, grab fresh seafood at a chiringuito (beach bar) on Barceloneta. Budget ~€15–20.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner near Palau de la Música — try 'Bar Brutal' in El Born for natural wines and creative small plates. Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Palau de la Música concert tickets well in advance — popular performances sell out fast in summer. The food tour typically starts around 10:00–11:00 AM; confirm timing when booking. Dress smart-casual for the evening concert.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to Park Güell (Gaudí's whimsical hilltop park) — book timed entry tickets online in advance. Explore the monumental zone with its mosaic terraces, dragon staircase, and Hypostyle Room, all offering sweeping views over Barcelona. Spend about 1.5–2 hours exploring. Afterward, stroll through the Gràcia neighborhood at the park's base — a charming bohemian district with independent boutiques and cafés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (La Pedrera) on Passeig de Gràcia — two of Gaudí's most spectacular residential buildings. Both offer audio-guided tours of the interiors and rooftop terraces. Casa Milà's rooftop warrior chimneys are iconic. Choose one (or both if time allows). Passeig de Gràcia itself is a great spot for window-shopping at high-street and designer stores.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Barcelona's legendary nightlife along Passeig Marítim — the Clubbing on Passeig Marítim experience. Start with sunset drinks at a rooftop bar near Port Olímpic, then visit iconic beachfront clubs like Pacha or Opium as the night progresses. Clubs typically get lively after midnight and stay open until dawn.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast in Gràcia neighborhood near Park Güell — try 'La Pepita' for avocado toast and specialty coffee. Budget ~€10–14.
meals.lunch: Lunch on Passeig de Gràcia — try 'Cervecería Catalana' for excellent tapas and montaditos (small open sandwiches). Budget ~€18–25.
meals.dinner: Early dinner near Port Olímpic before the nightlife begins — try fresh seafood paella or fideuà at a beachfront restaurant. Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell timed tickets are mandatory for the monumental zone — book at least a week ahead in August. For clubbing, dress smart (no flip-flops or sportswear). Cover charges range €15–25 and often include one drink. Pace yourself — Barcelona nightlife runs very late!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in after the late night! Enjoy a slow, relaxed morning — have a late breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café. Take a final leisurely walk along Barceloneta Beach and the W Barcelona waterfront. Browse the Mercat de Santa Caterina (a colorful alternative to the touristy La Boqueria) for fresh produce, local cheeses, and artisan goods — a wonderful final morning market experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Picasso Museum in El Born (book tickets online to skip queues) — one of the most important collections of Pablo Picasso's work, housed in five medieval palaces. The museum traces his early development and features masterpieces from his Blue Period. Allow 1.5–2 hours. Afterward, do any last-minute souvenir shopping in El Born or the Gothic Quarter.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a special mid-range restaurant to celebrate the trip. Then enjoy a final evening stroll along the illuminated Barceloneta promenade and beachfront — soak in the warm Mediterranean night air one last time before preparing for departure.

meals.breakfast: Late brunch at a beachfront café — try eggs, pan con tomate, and fresh fruit juice. Budget ~€12–16.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Picasso Museum — try 'El Xampanyet' again or explore a new spot in El Born. Budget ~€15–20.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at 'Parking Pizza' (creative Neapolitan-style pizzas in a cool setting) or splurge slightly at 'Bodega Sepúlveda' for traditional Catalan cuisine. Budget ~€28–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure flight is later in the day. The Picasso Museum is closed on Mondays — Day 5 falls on a Thursday so this works perfectly. Keep the evening relaxed if you have an early flight the next morning.

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30. Private chauffeur transfer arranged from Barcelona El Prat Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort, Beachfront. Enjoy a seamless VIP check-in with welcome amenities prepared by the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival welcome: Unwind with a curated welcome amenity in your suite — chilled cava, seasonal fruit, and a personalized note from the concierge. Take a short stroll along the moonlit beachfront promenade directly accessible from the resort to decompress after the flight.

meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining from the resort's premium 24-hour menu — recommended: Iberian charcuterie board, pan con tomate, and a glass of Priorat red wine to ease into Barcelona's culinary scene.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag management is key for a luxury experience. Confirm next-day reservations with the concierge upon check-in. Request a beachfront-facing suite for optimal views. Private transfer should be pre-booked and confirmed before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Skip-the-Line Guided Tour (9:00 AM): Begin the day with a private guided tour of Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica. Marvel at the interplay of light through the stained-glass windows, explore the Nativity and Passion facades in depth, and ascend one of the towers for panoramic city views. A private guide ensures an intimate, unhurried experience with architectural commentary tailored to enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour (2:00 PM): After a leisurely lunch, dive into Barcelona's medieval core. Explore Roman ruins beneath the city streets, the Gothic Cathedral of Barcelona, and hidden plazas like Plaça de Sant Felip Neri. A private guide will reveal centuries of layered history and architectural evolution from Roman Barcino to medieval Gothic splendor.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Concert (8:00 PM): Attend a live performance inside this breathtaking UNESCO-listed Modernista concert hall designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. The explosion of stained glass, sculptural detail, and acoustic brilliance makes this an unmissable architectural and cultural experience. Reserve premium orchestra-level seats in advance.

meals.breakfast: In-resort breakfast at the Aegean Bliss Resort's terrace restaurant — à la carte selection featuring eggs Benedict, fresh-pressed juices, pastries, and Catalan-style pa amb tomàquet with jamón ibérico.
meals.lunch: Alkimia (Michelin-starred) near the Eixample district — Chef Jordi Vilà's refined take on modern Catalan cuisine. Opt for the tasting menu with wine pairing for a mid-day indulgence.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Casa Calvet Restaurant, housed inside a Gaudí-designed building — elegant Catalan cuisine with dishes like duck confit with truffle sauce and seasonal seafood. Reserve the private dining room for an exclusive experience.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tower access separately as it sells out quickly, especially in August. The Gothic Quarter tour is best in the early afternoon when crowds thin slightly. Dress smart-casual for the Palau de la Música concert — the venue has a refined ambiance. Arrange a private car between all venues for seamless transitions.

day_by_day.morning: Private Architectural Walking Tour of the Eixample District (9:30 AM): Embark on a bespoke private tour of Barcelona's iconic grid-planned Eixample neighborhood, focusing on Modernista masterpieces. Visit Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) with skip-the-line VIP access, and explore the lesser-known gems like Casa Lleó Morera and Casa Amatller along the Manzana de la Discordia block. A private architectural historian guide provides expert context on Gaudí, Domènech i Montaner, and Puig i Cadafalch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell Private Experience (2:30 PM): Explore Gaudí's whimsical hilltop park with a private guide. Wander the monumental zone's mosaic terraces, the Hypostyle Room, and enjoy sweeping panoramic views over Barcelona and the Mediterranean. Opt for a VIP early-access or off-peak slot to minimize crowds in the August heat.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Cocktails & Clubbing on Passeig Marítim (9:00 PM onwards): Begin the evening with sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the Mediterranean — W Barcelona's Eclipse Bar is ideal for pre-night drinks with breathtaking sea views. Then immerse yourself in Barcelona's legendary beachfront nightlife: visit Pacha Barcelona or Opium for a premium clubbing experience with VIP table reservations arranged in advance. The beachfront location makes it easy to return to the Aegean Bliss Resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast with a focus on energy — acai bowls, smoked salmon platters, and freshly brewed single-origin coffee on the terrace overlooking the sea.
meals.lunch: Disfrutar Restaurant (two Michelin stars) — one of Barcelona's most celebrated avant-garde dining experiences. Chef Oriol Castro and team deliver a theatrical tasting menu of innovative Mediterranean cuisine. Book months in advance; confirm reservation upon arrival.
meals.dinner: Late dinner at KAIA Kaipe beachfront restaurant near Barceloneta — premium Basque-Catalan seafood including grilled turbot, txangurro (spider crab), and a curated Txakoli wine selection. Perfect pre-club dining with an atmospheric sea-facing terrace.

day_by_day.notes: August heat in Barcelona peaks in the afternoon — carry water and wear breathable clothing for Park Güell. VIP table reservations at Pacha or Opium should be arranged through the hotel concierge at least 2–3 days in advance. Dress code at premium clubs is smart-chic; avoid sportswear. Clubs typically peak between midnight and 4:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely Late Morning & Private Yacht Charter (11:00 AM): After a late start following the previous night's clubbing, enjoy a slow morning at the resort's beachfront pool. At 11:00 AM, board a private yacht charter departing from Port Olímpic (a short distance from the resort). Sail along the Barcelona coastline, taking in the city skyline from the sea, stopping for a swim in secluded coves, and enjoying champagne on deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tapas and Wine Tour in El Born (4:00 PM): Return from the yacht and freshen up before joining a private guided food tour through the trendy El Born neighborhood. Sample traditional Catalan tapas — patatas bravas, croquetas de jamón, boquerones, and pan amb tomàquet — paired with local vermouth and natural wines. Explore the neighborhood's stunning 19th-century iron market (Mercat de Santa Caterina) and boutique wine bars.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive Rooftop Dinner & Second Night of Nightlife (9:00 PM): Dine at the rooftop restaurant of the Mandarin Oriental Barcelona — Moments (Michelin-starred) — for refined Catalan haute cuisine with city views. Afterward, experience a different facet of Barcelona nightlife: visit Sala Apolo in the Poble Sec district for a more eclectic, culturally rich club experience, or return to the Passeig Marítim strip for a second night at CDLC (Carpe Diem Lounge Club) with VIP beachfront seating.

meals.breakfast: Late resort brunch (10:00 AM) — eggs royale, avocado toast with Cantabrian anchovies, fresh tropical fruit, and mimosas on the beachfront terrace.
meals.lunch: Champagne and premium canapés served on the private yacht — curated by the yacht charter company with fresh seafood, artisan cheeses, and Catalan charcuterie.
meals.dinner: Moments Restaurant at Mandarin Oriental Barcelona — Chef Raül Balam's tasting menu celebrating Catalan culinary heritage with refined modern technique. Exceptional wine cellar with sommelier-guided pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Private yacht charters in August should be booked at least a week in advance through the hotel concierge or a specialist like Yacht Charter Barcelona. Apply high-SPF sunscreen for the yacht excursion. The El Born food tour is best enjoyed at a leisurely pace — allow 2.5 to 3 hours. Confirm Moments restaurant reservation well in advance as it is highly sought after.

day_by_day.morning: Montjuïc & Pavilion Mies van der Rohe (10:00 AM): Take a private cable car or chauffeured ride up to Montjuïc hill for a final architectural highlight — the iconic Barcelona Pavilion by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, a landmark of 20th-century modernist architecture. Explore the pavilion's iconic Barcelona Chair, travertine planes, and reflective pools. Continue to the nearby Fundació Joan Miró for a curated private viewing of its world-class collection in a stunning rationalist building by Josep Lluís Sert.
